patients.summary: Retired postal supervisor with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and well-suppressed HIV who joins in 2018. Over the next years he is diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma and Alzheimer's disease, has an inferior STEMI complicated by a post-infarction VSD needing surgical repair, a right ACA stroke with full recovery, an acute left angle-closure attack and a concussion from a fall on ice.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Toussaint phoned looking for a new primary care doctor; his previous physician is retiring. He turned 65 in January and is on traditional Medicare with a Part D plan. Retired from the postal service. Gets his HIV care from an outside infectious disease clinic and wants to keep that arrangement. Membership explained, welcome packet mailed. Release of information for the prior practice signed at the window and faxed. First visit booked for July 10, 70 minutes, which covers the Medicare welcome exam.

documents.title: New Patient Visit / Initial Preventive Physical Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 y/o retired postal service supervisor establishing care; prior PCP retiring. Here alone, sharp historian.

PMH: hypertension for roughly 12 years, on three agents since before I met him. High cholesterol about 8 years, on atorvastatin. HIV diagnosed 2009; followed at an outside ID clinic, says his counts have been fine and the virus undetectable for years on a one-pill regimen. No hospitalizations. No heart disease, stroke or diabetes that he knows of.
PSH: none.
Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, aspirin 81 daily (his last doctor started it years ago), Biktarvy 1 tab daily from ID.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father had a heart attack at 61 and is deceased; mother developed Alzheimer's in her early 70s; one sister has open-angle glaucoma.
Social: married, lives with his wife. Smoked about a pack a day for 25 years, stopped in 2012. A couple of beers or a glass of wine a week. Walks most mornings. Retired from supervising a mail sorting facility.

ROS: negative. No chest pain, dyspnea, edema, vision complaints, memory complaints.

Exam: well-appearing. BP and pulse as recorded, repeated seated after 5 min. Fundi not well seen without dilation. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no pulsatile mass. No edema, pedal pulses 2+. Gait steady. Get-up-and-go normal. Hearing grossly intact. Vision screen per MA normal with glasses.

Welcome to Medicare elements: functional status independent, no falls in past year, home safety reviewed, advance directive discussed (none on file; he will think about it), PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Hypertension: at goal on lisinopril, amlodipine, metoprolol. Continue. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today on atorvastatin 40.
3. HIV: stable per patient, ID manages ART. Will request their last note and labs.
4. Former smoker, 25 pack-years, quit 6 years ago: meets lung screening criteria; shared decision discussion held, he wants it. Low-dose CT ordered.
5. AAA screen: one-time ultrasound ordered (male, ever smoker).
6. Prevention: hep C antibody once today. Colonoscopy per patient around 2016, normal; records requested. Flu and pneumococcal in the fall. Tdap status pending records.
7. Aspirin for primary prevention: he prefers to stay on it; no bleeding history. Revisit.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Toussaint, your blood work from Tuesday is back. Kidney function, liver tests, electrolytes and blood counts are normal. The hepatitis C test is negative. Your A1c is in the normal range, so no sign of diabetes. Cholesterol on the atorvastatin is reasonable and we'll keep the same dose. The ultrasound and lung CT will be scheduled by radiology; they should call you within the week.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records from prior primary care office received (112 pages) and indexed. Includes medication lists consistent with current meds, screening colonoscopy report 04/2016 (normal exam to the cecum, good prep, no polyps; 10-year interval suggested), Tdap 09/2014, and BP flowsheets 2013-2018 mostly in the 120s-130s systolic. No immunization record for pneumococcal or zoster vaccines. Forwarded to PCP inbox.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old records. Nothing unexpected. Colonoscopy 2016 normal, next 2026. Tdap 2014 counts. Updated health maintenance. Needs PCV13 this fall, then PPSV23 a year later, and Shingrix.

reports.text: Limited abdominal ultrasound for aortic aneurysm screening. The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximum anteroposterior outer-to-outer diameter 2.1 cm in the infrarenal segment. No focal dilation, no mural thrombus. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Baseline lung cancer screening CT, low-dose technique, no contrast. Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. No emphysema. Airways patent. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Ultrasound and CT results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Mr. Toussaint, the doctor reviewed both scans from yesterday. The aorta ultrasound is normal, no aneurysm, and that one never needs repeating. The lung screening CT is clear. We'll repeat the lung CT each year around this time. Let us know if you have questions.

documents.title: Infectious disease clinic letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: Thank you for taking over primary care for Mr. Toussaint, whom we follow for HIV infection diagnosed in 2009. He has had a suppressed viral load since 2011 on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide, tolerating it well with excellent adherence. Visit 08/14/2018: no complaints. Labs: CD4 610 cells/mm3, HIV-1 RNA below 20 copies/mL. Renal function normal. Plan: continue current regimen, labs and visit yearly, sooner if needed. He has no known drug allergies. We will send notes after each visit.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for fall vaccines per PCP. Screening questions negative. High-dose flu given left deltoid, PCV13 right deltoid. VIS sheets given. Observed 15 minutes without reaction. Reminded PPSV23 due one year from now.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: renewal request for metoprolol succinate 50 mg and amlodipine 5 mg, 90-day supplies. Last seen 07/2018, BP at goal. Sent per protocol with 3 refills each. Atorvastatin and lisinopril still have refills on file.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6-month check. Feels well. Taking all meds, no missed doses. Home BP cuff readings mostly 120s/70s. Still walking, less in the cold. ID visit in August went fine.
O: vitals reviewed. Heart regular, lungs clear, no ankle swelling.
A/P: HTN controlled, no change. HLD on atorvastatin 40, July lipids acceptable. BMP today for the ACE inhibitor. Mentions an eye appointment coming up for cloudy vision in the right eye; he'll have the eye doctor send notes. Wellness visit in July.

documents.title: Ophthalmology letter: cataract
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Dear colleague, I saw Mr. Toussaint on 04/23/2019 for gradual blurring and glare in the right eye over the past year, worse with night driving. Best corrected acuity reduced on the right, good on the left. Intraocular pressures within normal limits both eyes. Dense nuclear cataract right eye; left lens with minimal change. Dilated fundus exam unremarkable as far as can be seen on the right. Plan: right cataract extraction with lens implant, scheduled 06/11/2019. Please complete a pre-operative history and physical within 30 days of surgery. Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. Normal intervals and axis. No ST or T wave abnormality. No Q waves.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Pre-operative H&P
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op H&P for right cataract extraction with IOL, 06/11/2019, monitored anesthesia care.

Hx: HTN, HLD, HIV suppressed on ART. No cardiac or pulmonary disease. Climbs two flights without stopping; walks 2 miles. No chest pain, dyspnea, syncope. No bleeding problems. No prior anesthesia.
Meds unchanged from list. NKDA.
Exam: BP and HR as charted. Heart regular without murmur, lungs clear, airway unremarkable.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no abnormalities.
Labs: BMP and CBC sent, will forward.

Assessment: low-risk procedure in a patient with good functional capacity. No further cardiac testing needed. OK to continue aspirin per ophthalmology preference. Take morning BP meds with a sip of water. Medically optimized. Faxed to surgical center.

documents.title: Operative report: right cataract extraction
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Date of surgery 06/11/2019. Procedure: phacoemulsification of right cataract with posterior chamber intraocular lens in the capsular bag. Anesthesia: topical with monitored sedation. Findings: dense nuclear sclerotic cataract. Uncomplicated; capsule intact. Patient tolerated well. Post-op drops per surgical center protocol for 4 weeks. Post-op day 1: acuity improved, pressure normal, clear cornea. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First Medicare AWV. Right eye much better since the June surgery; says colors look brighter. No new complaints.

Health risk assessment reviewed: independent in all daily activities, drives, manages his own pills with a weekly box. No falls. Wears seatbelt. Smoke detectors at home. Hearing fine. Mood good, PHQ-2 0. No concerns about memory raised by patient or wife.

Exam: BP, pulse, weight as charted; BMI stable. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

Plan / prevention schedule:
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.
- PPSV23 and flu at an October nurse visit. Shingrix: he'll start the series at his pharmacy.
- Lung screening CT due in September.
- Colonoscopy next due 2026.
- Continue current medications. Advance directive forms given again.
Follow up in 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from your wellness visit look good. Blood counts, kidneys and liver are normal. Cholesterol is about where it was last year. Keep everything the same.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization record
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Notice of vaccine administered at community pharmacy: recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1 of 2, 08/16/2019, left deltoid. Patient advised to return for dose 2 in 2 to 6 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT compared with 08/2018. No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear without consolidation. No pleural effusion. Normal heart size. No lymphadenopathy.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening CT negative again, Lung-RADS 1. Letter mailed. Repeat 1 year.

documents.title: Infectious disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: Annual HIV visit 09/10/2019. Doing well, no missed doses, no opportunistic infections. Recent cataract surgery noted. CD4 590 cells/mm3, viral load not detected (<20). Creatinine stable. Continue bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF. Return in one year. NKDA.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines today per standing plan: high-dose influenza L deltoid, PPSV23 R deltoid, Shingrix #2 L deltoid (lower site, 1 inch apart). Dose 1 was at pharmacy in August. Tolerated. Waited 15 min. Warned arm may ache and he may feel run down for a day with the shingles shot. Pneumococcal series now complete.

documents.title: Mail order question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My insurance wants me to switch my blood pressure pills to the mail order pharmacy. Do you need to send new prescriptions or do they take care of it?

documents.title: RE: Mail order question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: We'll send new prescriptions to the mail order pharmacy today for lisinopril, amlodipine, metoprolol and atorvastatin, 90 days with refills. Keep using your local pharmacy until the first shipment arrives. Your HIV medicine comes from the ID clinic so they would handle that one.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Progressive loss of peripheral vision; sister with glaucoma

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine BP visit, but the main thing today is vision. Since about last fall he has been clipping door frames and the corner of the kitchen table, and his wife noticed he startles when people approach from the side. Reading and TV are fine. Right eye was done for cataract last June and the central vision there is good. Occasional mild ache around the eyes in dim rooms. No sudden loss of vision, no flashes, no floaters, no headache.

Sister has open-angle glaucoma.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. Confrontation fields: he misses fingers in the outer quadrants on both sides. Central acuity with glasses good in each eye. Undilated fundi limited.

A/P
1. Peripheral field loss, bilateral, gradual. Concern for glaucoma given family history. Ophthalmology referral placed, asked for a prompt appointment. Advised extra caution driving, particularly at intersections, until he is seen.
2. HTN: at goal. BMP.
3. HLD, HIV: no change.
RTC 4-6 months.

documents.title: Medication supply and scheduling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called patient re: pandemic office changes. He and his wife are staying home. Has about 6 weeks of all meds; we sent early 90-day fills to mail order so he won't run short. Ophthalmology office called him to postpone his eye appointment, no new date yet. Advised to call us if vision changes suddenly. Spring follow-up will be by video.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his kitchen, wife helping with the tablet; consent for telehealth given. Home BP readings this month 118-132 / 70-80, pulse 60s. Feels fine, no fever or cough, staying in. Vision about the same, still bumping the occasional door frame. Ophthalmology rescheduled him for May 18.
Assessment: HTN controlled at home. Field loss pending eye exam. Continue current meds. Will see in person in summer for the wellness visit.

medications.sig: Instill 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
medications.reason: Primary open-angle glaucoma; prescribed by ophthalmology

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Re: Jerome Toussaint, DOB 01/07/1953. Seen 05/18/2020 at your request.

He describes roughly eight months of steadily narrowing side vision: walking into furniture at home and, while driving, not noticing people on the sidewalk unless they are right ahead of him. There is an intermittent mild discomfort in both eyes that seems to come on in dim light. He denies any abrupt drop in vision, flashing lights or new floaters. Sister has POAG. Right eye pseudophakic since 06/2019. Medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and HIV on ART. NKDA.

Exam: central vision intact in both eyes. Intraocular pressure 27 mm Hg right and 27 mm Hg left by applanation. Anterior segments quiet; right IOL well centered. Dilated fundus: enlarged cupping of both optic discs, no disc hemorrhages, no exudates; maculae and periphery otherwise normal.
Humphrey 24-2 visual fields: marked peripheral constriction in both eyes with sparing of fixation.

Impression: primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes, advanced field loss.
Plan: start latanoprost 0.005% one drop both eyes at bedtime. Recheck pressure in 6 weeks, then every few months. We discussed that lost field does not come back and the importance of nightly drops. He was advised about driving given the field results. Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Pharmacy fill notice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fill history update from pharmacy: latanoprost 0.005% 2.5 mL filled 05/19/2020, prescriber ophthalmology. Added to medication list. Consult letter not yet received, will watch for it.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit. Saw ophthalmology in May: glaucoma in both eyes with significant field loss; on latanoprost nightly, pressure check went well per patient.

HRA: independent in ADLs, wife keeps the calendar. No falls. Mood fine, PHQ-2 0. He has no concerns about his memory today.
Meds reconciled: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, Biktarvy, latanoprost OU qhs.

Exam: vitals as charted. Cardiopulmonary exam unremarkable, no edema.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids. Lung CT in September. Flu shot in October. Glaucoma per ophthalmology. Next visit in 4 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual screening CT. Comparison 09/2019. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or adenopathy. Cardiac size within normal limits.

documents.title: LDCT 2020
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative screening CT. Annual repeat.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Curbside flu vaccine clinic. High-dose influenza R deltoid. No reaction. Wife accompanied.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Glaucoma follow-up 11/12/2020. Using latanoprost nightly, his wife puts the drops in. Pressures 18 mm Hg right and 18 left, down from 27. Discs unchanged. Repeat fields in the spring. Continue latanoprost. Return 6 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office visit: memory
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his daughter, who asked for this visit; fasting labs drawn this morning before the appointment.

She describes a slow change since around the start of the year: he repeats questions, has trouble working out problems he used to handle easily (the checkbook, a leaky faucet), and twice this fall he got turned around inside the house looking for the bathroom at night. His wife has taken over the bills. He minimizes it, says he just forgets names. No falls, no head injury, no new medicines, no hallucinations, no tremor. Mood flat at times but he denies feeling sad; PHQ-9 3. Mother had Alzheimer's starting in her 70s. HIV suppressed for years per ID.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pleasant, a little withdrawn, lets daughter answer. Clearly struggles to recall recent events in conversation; formal testing left to neurology. Cranial nerves grossly normal, strength full, gait normal.

A/P
1. Progressive cognitive decline over about a year with functional impact. Labs today for reversible contributors: CMP, CBC, B12, TSH. Neurology referral for formal evaluation; daughter will come to that visit. Safety: discussed stove and medication supervision; wife will fill his pill box.
2. HTN, HLD stable. Glaucoma followed by ophthalmology.
Short follow-up after neurology.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sending this to your proxy account as requested. All of Tuesday's labs are normal: fasting sugar 98, kidney function normal (creatinine 1.0), liver tests normal, blood counts normal, B12 and thyroid normal. That means we have not found a simple fixable cause, which is why the neurology visit matters. Their office should call within two weeks.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. This is his daughter writing. Neurology called and gave us January 8, the earliest they had. We'll bring the list of things we've noticed.

documents.title: Infectious disease annual note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: Visit 11/10/2020 (in clinic). Remains adherent on bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF; daughter now helps with pill organization. Viral load below 20 copies/mL, CD4 600 cells/mm3. We are aware of the cognitive concerns and the planned neurology evaluation; with a decade of continuous suppression, HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder is less likely but neurology will weigh it. Continue regimen. Next visit in one year.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Reason for consultation: memory decline. Seen 01/08/2021 with his daughter.

Mr. Toussaint is a 68-year-old man with treated hypertension and hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART with a viral load undetectable for about ten years, and glaucoma diagnosed by ophthalmology last spring. His daughter reports a year of worsening short-term memory, difficulty reasoning through everyday problems and episodes of disorientation in his own home. He has taken his antiretroviral regimen faithfully.
Medications: lisinopril, amlodipine, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, aspirin, Biktarvy, latanoprost. NKDA.
Family history: mother with Alzheimer's disease from age 72.

Exam: awake and alert, flat affect with apathy. Struggles to recount recent events and loses track partway through serial sevens. MMSE 20/30. Language fluent. Cranial nerves intact. No weakness, normal tone. Gait normal.
Data reviewed from referring office and ID: CD4 600, HIV RNA <20, CBC normal, fasting glucose 98, creatinine 1.0, liver tests normal, B12 and TSH normal.

Impression: dementia of the Alzheimer type, mild to moderate, with a strong family history. Sustained viral suppression makes HIV-related cognitive disorder unlikely.
Plan: donepezil 5 mg at bedtime for 4 weeks, then 10 mg if tolerated; our nurse will call. Supervision of medications and finances. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Question about donepezil
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, it's his daughter again. Dad started the donepezil last week. Does it matter what time of day he takes it? Mom has been giving it with his bedtime eye drops.

documents.title: RE: Question about donepezil
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Bedtime is how neurology prescribed it, so pairing it with the eye drops is a good routine. Call us if he gets dizzy, vomits, or his pulse on the home cuff runs below 50, since he also takes metoprolol. Neurology's nurse will call about the dose increase in a few weeks.

documents.title: Neurology nurse telephone note
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Spoke with patient's daughter. Four weeks on donepezil 5 mg without side effects. No falls or dizziness. Increasing to 10 mg daily per plan; new prescription sent. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: COVID vaccines from state registry
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Reconciled state immunization registry: Moderna COVID-19 vaccine doses 02/04/2021 and 03/04/2021 given at a regional vaccination site. Primary series complete.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit with patient, wife and daughter on the line. Neurology diagnosed Alzheimer's dementia in January; now on donepezil 10 mg since February, tolerating it. Family thinks he is maybe a little more engaged in the evenings. Home BP 120s-130s/70s, pulse 58-66, no lightheadedness. Both COVID vaccines done.

Assessment and plan:
- Alzheimer's disease on donepezil: continue; watch pulse given metoprolol plus donepezil, home readings fine.
- HTN: controlled.
- Glaucoma: wife doing the drops nightly.
- Talked about naming a health care agent; daughter willing. Will formalize at the summer wellness visit.
RTC July.

documents.title: Refill renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail order requested renewals for atorvastatin 40 and lisinopril 20. Sent, 90 days x 3. Donepezil is through neurology and latanoprost through ophthalmology, both have active refills per fill history.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Follow-up 07/13/2021 with daughter. On donepezil 10 mg for five months, no side effects now. Family reports he is stable, maybe slightly more interactive. MMSE 20/30, unchanged from January. Neuro exam nonfocal, gait normal. Plan: continue donepezil 10 mg. Discussed home safety and future planning. Return in 12 months or sooner with change.

events.reason: Annual wellness visit and advance care planning

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit with advance care planning
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife and daughter present.

Interval: neurology follow-up this month, MMSE unchanged at 20, donepezil continues. Glaucoma pressures controlled per ophthalmology. No ED visits.
Function: bathes and dresses himself, needs reminders. Wife handles meds and money. No falls. Sleeps well. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, oriented to person and place, not date. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Gait steady.

Advance care planning (30 min, voluntary, patient participating): he chose his daughter as health care agent, wife as alternate. Health care proxy form completed and scanned. He says he would want treatment for things that can be fixed but not to be kept alive on machines if he no longer recognized his family. MOLST not completed at this time.

Plan: labs. Lung CT in September. Flu and COVID booster in fall when available. Continue all meds. 6 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT, comparison 09/2020. No nodules. No airspace disease. No effusion. Heart and mediastinum normal.

documents.title: LDCT 2021
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung-RADS 1 again. Results letter sent to patient and proxy.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife with patient. High-dose influenza L deltoid; Moderna booster (half dose) R deltoid. Eligible by age, more than 6 months since primary series. Tolerated, observed 15 minutes.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Seen 11/09/2021 with his wife. IOP 17 right, 17 left on latanoprost. Optic nerves stable. Visual fields repeated and compared with 2020: stable constriction, no progression. Continue latanoprost at bedtime. Follow up in one year, sooner for any eye pain or vision change.

documents.title: Infectious disease annual note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: HIV visit 11/16/2021 with daughter. Now on donepezil for Alzheimer's disease; no interactions with bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF. Adherence supervised by family. CD4 640 cells/mm3, viral load not detected. Continue ART, return 12 months.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 2:40 follow-up. Called home; wife said the appointment was not on their calendar and apologized. Rebooked for February. Added daughter as second reminder contact.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from December. With wife. No new problems. Memory about the same per wife, keeps busy with yard plans for spring and church on weekends. Takes meds from the weekly box she fills. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no swelling.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear.
A/P: HTN at goal on current regimen. Lipids and BMP today. Alzheimer's stable on donepezil. Glaucoma stable per November letter. Next visit summer for AWV.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his wife. The mail order says the amlodipine prescription ran out of refills. Can you renew it?

conditions.label: ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction involving right coronary artery

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 110. ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF.

Portable AP chest. Bilateral perihilar and basilar airspace opacities with interstitial thickening and vascular congestion. Cardiac silhouette at upper limits of normal for technique. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit 05/26/2022, received by fax.

69-year-old man brought by ambulance. About two hours before arrival he became acutely short of breath while cutting the grass, with palpitations and inability to lie flat. Denies chest pain. History: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, open-angle glaucoma, Alzheimer's dementia. No known coronary disease. NKDA.

Triage: BP 150/90, HR 110, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air.
Exam: in respiratory distress, speaking in short phrases. Crackles to the mid lung fields bilaterally. JVD present. New holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating toward the axilla. No leg edema.
ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF. Troponin I 10 ng/mL (reference <0.04). Portable chest film with pulmonary edema.

Course: STEMI alert at 16:52. Aspirin 324 mg chewed, heparin bolus, IV furosemide, noninvasive ventilation. Cardiology at bedside; to the cath lab at 17:55.
Diagnoses: acute inferior STEMI; acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema.

documents.title: Discharge summary: inferior STEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admitted 05/26/2022, discharged 05/29/2022.

Principal diagnosis: acute inferior ST-elevation MI. Secondary: acute decompensated heart failure, resolved; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; HIV on ART; Alzheimer's dementia; primary open-angle glaucoma.

Catheterization 05/26: right radial access. Right coronary artery occluded in its mid segment, culprit. Left main, LAD and circumflex without significant stenosis. Thrombectomy not needed; one drug-eluting stent to the mid RCA with TIMI 3 flow restored. No complications.
Course: diuresed overnight, off noninvasive ventilation by the next morning, on room air from day 2. Telemetry without sustained arrhythmia. Walked the halls on day 3 without symptoms.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; clopidogrel 75 mg daily (new, for at least 12 months after the stent); metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; Biktarvy daily; latanoprost both eyes nightly; donepezil 10 mg daily. NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiology 6-8 weeks; PCP 1-2 weeks. Return for chest pain or breathlessness.

reports.text: Limited bedside study. Dilated left ventricle. Color flow demonstrates a jet across the interventricular septum consistent with a ventricular septal defect with left-to-right shunting.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 05/31/2022.

Returned five days after admission for inferior STEMI with RCA stent; discharged two days ago on aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol and atorvastatin with his usual medicines. This morning at rest he developed sudden breathlessness, chest pain and a racing heartbeat.

Vitals: BP 85/50, HR 122, RR 28.
Exam: diaphoretic, distressed. Rales at both bases. Loud harsh holosystolic murmur at the left sternal border with a palpable thrill. JVP elevated.
Labs: troponin I elevated; BNP markedly elevated; creatinine 1.2 (baseline 1.0); hemoglobin 13.2; WBC 12,000.
ECG: inferior Q waves, as on discharge. Bedside echo: dilated LV with flow across the ventricular septum.

Assessment: post-infarction ventricular septal rupture with cardiogenic shock.
Course: vasopressor support started, cardiothoracic surgery consulted, transferred to the tertiary cardiac surgery center at 10:20.

documents.title: Discharge summary: VSD repair
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Tertiary cardiac surgery center. Admitted 05/31/2022 in transfer, discharged 06/13/2022 home with services.

Diagnosis: post-infarction ventricular septal defect after inferior STEMI (RCA stent 05/26/2022), with cardiogenic shock and acute decompensated heart failure.

Operation 06/01/2022: surgical patch repair of the inferoseptal ventricular septal defect on cardiopulmonary bypass. Intraoperative TEE after repair: no residual shunt. Clopidogrel held before surgery and resumed on postoperative day 3.
Postoperative course: extubated day 1, vasopressors weaned by day 3, chest tubes out day 4. Diuresed to dry weight. Ambulating independently at discharge.
Discharge exam: sternal wound clean. No murmur. Lungs clear. Weight 82.0 kg.
Labs at discharge: creatinine back to 1.0, hemoglobin 12.5.

Discharge medications: unchanged from the 05/29 list: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20 (restarted day 6 once pressures recovered), amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10. NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiac surgery wound check 2 weeks; cardiology 6 weeks with echo; PCP within 1 week; cardiac rehab referral at cardiology visit. Sternal precautions 8 weeks.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after STEMI and VSD repair

documents.title: Transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 3 days after discharge; RN reached the family by phone on 06/14. Wife and daughter present.

Two admissions in three weeks: inferior STEMI 05/26 with RCA drug-eluting stent (presented with pulmonary edema), then on 05/31 a post-infarction VSD with shock, repaired surgically 06/01 at the tertiary center. Both discharge summaries reviewed.

Today: tired but walking around the house and to the mailbox. Mild sternal soreness. No chest pressure like before, no orthopnea, sleeping flat on two pillows (his usual). No palpitations. Appetite returning. Family says he is at his usual baseline.

Med reconciliation done with the bottles: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75 (new), metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10. Wife has the pill box set.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP soft-normal. Sternotomy healing, no drainage. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Weight 82.0 kg, matches discharge.

A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p RCA DES; post-infarction VSD s/p patch repair; recent decompensated heart failure, resolved. Doing well. Dual antiplatelet therapy for at least 12 months; stressed not stopping clopidogrel without cardiology. Sternal precautions. Daily weights, call for gain of 3 lb in a day or 5 in a week. BMP and CBC today.
2. HTN: at the low end on full regimen; if lightheaded, hold amlodipine and call.
3. Alzheimer's: family supervision continues.
4. Cardiology and cardiac surgery follow-ups are scheduled.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Labs from Thursday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium are normal. His blood count is a little low, which is expected a few weeks after heart surgery, and should recover on its own; we'll recheck at the next visit. No changes. Keep up the daily weights and let us know if they creep up.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Seen 07/19/2022 with his daughter, 7 weeks after inferior STEMI with mid-RCA DES and 6 weeks after surgical repair of a post-infarction VSD. Cleared at his surgical wound check. Walking 15 minutes twice a day, no angina, no dyspnea at that level, no palpitations.
Exam: BP and pulse well controlled; sternum healed; regular rhythm, no murmur; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: continue aspirin and clopidogrel through at least 05/2023; metoprolol, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril and amlodipine unchanged. Echo in 3 weeks. Referral to cardiac rehabilitation sent. Return in one year, sooner if needed.

reports.text: Complete study. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness. Hypokinesis of the inferior wall; remaining segments contract normally. LVEF 55% by biplane method. Patch in the inferior septum intact with no residual shunt by color flow. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Trace mitral regurgitation; papillary muscles intact. Other valves normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Intact VSD patch without residual shunt. LVEF 55% with inferior wall hypokinesis.

documents.title: Emergency department record

Regional hospital ED, 05/18/2023.

70-year-old man brought in by his wife, who saw him scuffing his left foot along the floor this afternoon. He has no pain and says the leg just will not lift right. Background: CAD with inferior MI and RCA stent 05/2022, post-MI VSD repaired, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, Alzheimer's dementia, glaucoma. No previous stroke or TIA. On aspirin and clopidogrel. NKDA.

Exam: alert and oriented. Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 in both arms and the right leg; left leg 3/5 with mildly increased tone. Sensation intact. Coordination and reflexes normal in the upper extremities.
CT head: acute right ACA territory infarct, no hemorrhage.

Impression: acute ischemic stroke, right anterior cerebral artery territory, first event. Admitted to the stroke unit.

documents.title: Discharge summary: ischemic stroke
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 05/18/2023, discharged 05/21/2023 home with wife.

Diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, right anterior cerebral artery territory, presenting with left leg weakness.
Course: neuro checks stable, no worsening. Continuous telemetry showed sinus rhythm throughout. Evaluated by physical therapy: safe for home with a rolling walker short term; outpatient PT arranged. Left leg strength 3+/5 at discharge, walking with walker and standby assist.
Medications: no changes. Continue aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10. NKDA.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 05/22/2024.

71-year-old man with open-angle glaucoma on latanoprost, right eye pseudophakic, brought by his daughter for abrupt, severe pain in the left eye starting about two hours before arrival, with a frontal headache, vomiting, blurred vision in that eye and rainbow-colored rings around lights. Light makes it worse and he cannot hold the left eye open. No injury, no fever, no discharge. Background: CAD with prior MI and stent, repaired post-MI VSD, prior stroke, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, Alzheimer's dementia. NKDA.

Exam: left eye red with marked conjunctival injection and tearing; pupil mid-dilated and nonreactive; cornea hazy; anterior chamber shallow. Right eye unremarkable. Tonometry: left IOP 38 mm Hg.

Assessment: acute angle-closure glaucoma, left eye.
Treatment: pressure-lowering eye drops and IV acetazolamide, antiemetic. Ophthalmology on call evaluated in the ED; pressure falling. Laser iridotomy arranged for the morning. Discharged to ophthalmology clinic.

documents.title: Daughter calling about ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called: father went to the ED Wednesday night with sudden left eye pain and was told it was an acute glaucoma attack. Ophthalmology did a laser procedure on the left eye yesterday. Pain gone, vision clearing, eating normally. She wanted us to know and asked if anything in his regular medicines could have caused it. Told her the eye team will review his list and we will look at the records when they arrive; no changes for now. Follow-up visit booked with PCP in June.

documents.title: Ophthalmology letter: acute angle closure
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Dear colleague, your patient presented to the ED on 05/22/2024 with acute angle-closure glaucoma of the left eye, IOP 38 mm Hg. After medical lowering in the ED, I performed a laser peripheral iridotomy of the left eye on 05/23/2024 without complication. The right eye is pseudophakic with a deep chamber and needs no laser.
Follow-up 05/30/2024: no pain, cornea clear, iridotomy patent, angle open on gonioscopy, left IOP 16 mm Hg. Acute attack resolved. Continue latanoprost both eyes at bedtime for his open-angle glaucoma. Post-laser drops completed. Return as previously scheduled, sooner for any recurrence of pain or halos. NKDA.

With wife. Quiet fall, no illnesses. Still in the cardiology study, next study visit in January. No chest pain, dyspnea, falls.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Walks steadily.
A/P: all stable; BMP today. Reminded family about icy steps and walkway salt this winter given prior stroke and dementia. RTC spring.

events.reason: Head injury after fall on ice

conditions.label: Concussion with loss of consciousness of 30 minutes or less, initial encounter

reports.text: Noncontrast head CT, comparison 05/2023. No acute intracranial hemorrhage. No skull fracture. Chronic encephalomalacia in the right anterior cerebral artery territory, consistent with the known prior infarct. No mass effect. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.
reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial abnormality. Chronic right ACA territory infarct.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 02/12/2026.

73-year-old man with Alzheimer's dementia and a prior stroke who fell backward on an icy front step this morning and struck the back of his head. He was out for a short time and was alert and answering within minutes. EMS reports he vomited twice on the way in. Here he is a little confused but oriented, with a dull headache that has eased over the past hour. Denies change in vision, seizure or weakness. On aspirin; no anticoagulant. Background also includes CAD with prior MI and stent, repaired VSD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, glaucoma. NKDA.

Exam: no focal neurological deficit; speech clear and coherent. Scalp without laceration. Neck nontender.
CT head without contrast: no hemorrhage or fracture; old right ACA infarct.

Observed for four hours: awake, cooperative and walking steadily at discharge, still somewhat tired.
Diagnosis: concussion with brief loss of consciousness.
Discharge: home with wife; head injury precautions; acetaminophen for headache; follow up with PCP within the week; return for worsening headache, repeated vomiting, new confusion or weakness.

documents.title: Wife calling after ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called: he slipped on the ice yesterday, hit his head and was seen in the ED, CT okay, told it was a concussion. Slept well with her checking on him overnight. Headache mild this morning, no vomiting since the ambulance, talking and walking as usual. Reviewed warning signs. Visit booked Tuesday with PCP.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for concussion

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife and daughter, five days after a fall on ice with brief loss of consciousness; ED diagnosed concussion, head CT without bleeding or fracture. ED record reviewed.
Since: headache faded to almost nothing, used acetaminophen twice. No vomiting. Family says he is back to his usual self cognitively, maybe a bit more tired the first few days. No new weakness or vision change.
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, conversant, at baseline per family. Cranial nerves intact, strength 5/5 all limbs, gait steady.
A/P
1. Concussion, improving. Rest and gradual return to usual walks. Return precautions reviewed. RN will call in a few weeks.
2. Fall prevention: the fall was a slip on ice rather than a balance problem; daughter arranging ice melt and a railing check on the front steps.
3. Other problems unchanged.
RTC June.

documents.title: Concussion check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called wife for planned check-in. No headache for over two weeks, no acetaminophen needed. Back to walking at the community center. Sleep and appetite normal. No further falls. Will see PCP in June.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. Concussion symptoms gone since early March. No further falls. Still in the cardiology study. Neurology visit was moved to the summer by their office. No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations. Eyes stable.
Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost OU nightly, donepezil 10, study drug (blinded).
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, at baseline. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Gait steady.
A/P
1. Concussion, resolved.
2. CAD with old inferior MI, VSD repaired; history of stroke without residual deficits: aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril, amlodipine. Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids.
3. HTN: at goal.
4. Alzheimer's disease: donepezil; family support in place.
5. POAG: ophthalmology yearly. HIV: ID yearly.
RTC September for follow-up; AWV after that.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Friday's labs are back. Kidney function, liver tests and blood counts are normal. The cholesterol panel is similar to his last ones. Nothing to change before his September visit.
